schema_version.description: Version of this schema the document was produced against, e.g. "1.1.0". Absent on documents produced before this field existed; consumers should treat a missing value as "1.0.0". Bump the minor version for additive, backward-compatible changes (new optional field, new enum value) and the major version for breaking changes.

xhr_endpoints.description: Optional XHR/fetch pairs intercepted during a headless crawl. Absent on older scans.

stats.description: Optional crawl metrics. Absent on older scans; not required.

category.description: "payload" covers all active payload-tester findings (SQLi/XSS/SSTI/path-traversal/SSRF/open-redirect/XXE); the specific vulnerability class is carried in the finding's "id" (e.g. payload-sql-error, payload-ssrf, payload-open-redirect), not a separate category value. "scan-note" is not a vulnerability; it is used to record that an active probe (e.g. CORS reflection, GraphQL introspection) was intentionally skipped, so consumers do not silently interpret an empty result as "checked, nothing found". "auth" covers authentication/session/authorization findings that aren't a single HTTP header or cookie -- missing rate limiting, session fixation, logout not invalidating the session, and cross-session/IDOR access -- again disambiguated by the finding's "id". "waf-challenge" flags a response that looks like a WAF/bot-mitigation challenge or interstitial page (Cloudflare, Akamai, PerimeterX, DataDome, a CAPTCHA wall, etc.) rather than real target content; when present, other checks against that same URL were not meaningfully performed. "smart-contract" is reserved for findings translated from Slither via slither-ingest; "sast" is reserved for findings folded in from an external SARIF file via report --merge-sarif.

confidence.description: Optional. How this finding was established: "confirmed" for an exact/unambiguous signal (an echoed marker string matched verbatim, a secret pattern matched literally), "probable" for a strong-but-inferential signal (blind/timing-based payload confirmation), "heuristic" for a passive check that flags a likely-but-unverified condition (a missing header, a suspicious comment). Absent on findings produced before this field existed or by checks that don't yet classify themselves.

cost_of_attack.description: Optional. How much an attacker needs beyond network access to exploit this: "none" (unauthenticated), "low" (a low-entropy/guessable token or a throwaway account), "medium" (a valid authenticated session), "high" (privileged/admin access or a high-entropy secret). A cross-cutting axis alongside severity, not a replacement for it.

minimal_repro.description: Optional. True when "evidence" holds the smallest payload variant found to still trigger this finding (binary-searched down from the full pack), rather than whichever payload happened to match first.

engines.description: Optional. Which crawler engine(s) independently reproduced this exact finding (same id+url) when a scan's results were merged via `shroodler compare-engines`. Two engines agreeing is a confidence signal; a single engine is not itself evidence of a false positive.

severity_disagreement.description: Optional. Set by `shroodler compare-engines` only when BOTH engines independently reproduced this (id, path, query) AND reported different severities -- lists the distinct severities each engine actually observed. Never set from one engine emitting the same key twice with different severities on its own.

owner.description: Optional. Team/individual responsible for remediating this finding, resolved from an ownership-rules file by `shroodler sla apply` (same id/url glob matching as .shroodlerignore).

first_seen.description: Optional. Date (YYYY-MM-DD) this finding (by id+url) first appeared in recorded scan history, set by `shroodler sla apply`. Null when history_available is false (not enough recorded history to determine this, NOT the same as 'first seen today').

age_days.description: Optional. Days since first_seen, set by `shroodler sla apply`. Null when first_seen is null.

sla_severity.description: Optional. Severity after SLA escalation (bumped up one level once age_days exceeds the SLA budget for the original severity, capped at critical). Equal to "severity" until the SLA burns down, and always equal to "severity" when history_available is false.

sla_breached.description: Optional. True once age_days has exceeded the SLA budget for this finding's original severity, set by `shroodler sla apply`. Always false when history_available is false -- absence of history is not evidence of a clean SLA.

history_available.description: Optional. False when `shroodler sla apply` found zero recorded scans for this target in history (missing/empty history dir, or wrong target) -- age_days/sla_breached could not be meaningfully evaluated, as opposed to being evaluated and clean.

pages_crawled.description: Number of pages recorded in pages[]

pages_challenged.description: Number of distinct URLs where a waf-challenge finding fired -- these pages were not meaningfully inspected (forms/secrets/JS-endpoints/etc. were not extracted from them). Absent on documents produced before this field existed; treat a missing value as 0. A high ratio of this against pages_crawled means the scan's other findings substantially understate the target's real attack surface.

requests.description: HTTP requests issued during the crawl, when counted

elapsed_ms.description: Wall time from crawl start to finish in milliseconds

stopped_reason.description: Why the crawl stopped enqueueing more work
